title: Sales enablement positioning and messaging, competitive briefs, pitch deck guidance, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a single, customer-facing sales enablement reference that the field can use for early discovery, technical validation, procurement conversations, and security reviews.
- Includes: positioning and messaging, competitive brief, pitch deck outline and slide-level talking points, practical pricing guidance, short case studies with metrics, and an FAQ for security-conscious prospects.

Who should use this doc
- Account executives and SDRs for discovery
- Solutions engineers for technical validation and demos
- Sales leadership for deal coaching and pricing exceptions
- Customer success for onboarding and expansion conversations

Positioning and core messaging
- Core one-liner: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM serving predictable, cost-effective, and production-ready across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

- Value pillars (short bullets to use in pitch)
  - Production-first performance: predictable p99 latency targets, continuous batching, and KV caching to meet real-time SLAs.
  - Cost controls and observability: token-level cost breakdowns, batching/quantization guidance, and per-route analytics.
  - Deployment flexibility: hosted API for fast time-to-value, dedicated capacity for committed throughput, and private VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads.
  - Reliability and graceful degradation: multi-variant routing and automatic fallbacks to maintain availability during capacity constraints.

- Elevator pitch (15-30s)
  - "Redwood gives engineering teams a single runtime to serve LLMs with predictable latency and unit cost across cloud and private deployments. We combine high-throughput GPU serving, smart batching and caching, and operational tooling so teams can ship faster without building custom inference stacks."

Common buyer objections and rebuttals
- Objection: "We can run inference ourselves to save money."
  - Rebuttal: Running inference in production incurs hidden costs (SRE time, monitoring, rollouts, regressions). Redwood reduces unit cost via batching/quantization recommendations while providing SLO-backed reliability and auditability.
- Objection: "We need full data control for compliance."
  - Rebuttal: Private deployment option provides on-prem or VPC control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs - meeting common compliance requirements.
- Objection: "Your pricing is opaque."
  - Rebuttal: We provide clear per-token and committed-capacity pricing examples, cost modeling templates, and an engagement to pilot cost optimization within 30 days.

Competitive brief (one-page summary for quick prep)
- Primary competitors to position against
  - CloudAI Endpoints (major public cloud managed endpoints)
  - InferenceX (specialized inference runtime vendor)
  - LLM-API-Provider (hosted-first LLM API provider)

- Differentiators to emphasize vs each competitor
  - Vs CloudAI Endpoints: Better developer ergonomics for inference at scale, deterministic SLOs for p50/p95/p99, and opinionated cost controls (batching, cache policies) tuned for LLM workloads.
  - Vs InferenceX: Redwood offers a full product surface (hosted, dedicated, private) plus first-class observability and rollouts; InferenceX is runtime-only and leaves orchestration to the customer.
  - Vs LLM-API-Provider: Redwood focuses on production economics and deployment flexibility rather than model access alone - customers can choose open models, quantized variants, or private models.

- Standard battlecards (talking points to use in live deals)
  - Win themes: predictable cost/performance, enterprise controls (SLA, audit logging, RBAC), integrated rollout patterns (canary/A-B/fallback).
  - Lose themes: if a prospect prefers one-off model experiments with no operational constraints, hosted-first providers may win on convenience. Use a short pilot to surface production issues.

Pitch deck recommended structure and slide-level talking points
1) Title & Hook
  - One-sentence problem statement and Redwood one-liner
2) The problem
  - Bullet examples: spiky traffic, unpredictable token costs, model quality regressions during rollouts, compliance requirements for regulated data.
3) Our solution
  - Diagram: Serving runtime + orchestration + console; mention features: batching, KV caching, quantization recommendations, routing policies.
4) How it works (technical high-level)
  - Describe runtime, kernel selection, and smart routing in 3 bullets.
5) Deployment modes & customer fit
  - Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private deployment (VPC & on-prem).
6) Observability & ops
  - Show console screenshots (or placeholders): per-route latency, token cost, traces, error analysis.
7) Pricing and procurement options
  - Show representative pricing table (example below) and call out pilot programs.
8) Case studies (2-3 short wins)
  - One-liner outcomes + KPIs (cost reduction, latency improvement, time-to-production).
9) Security & compliance
  - List certs, KMS integration, network isolation, logging.
10) Next steps / pilot offer
  - Suggested next steps: pilot scope, technical POC, procurement contacts, timeline.

Representative pricing guidance (use during early procurement conversations)
- Guiding principles
  - Provide both per-use (hosted) and committed (dedicated) pricing options.
  - Include 90-day pilot pricing and a migration plan to committed capacity.
  - Offer cost modeling: tokens per request, average seq length, concurrent QPS to estimate monthly spend.

- Example pricing (illustrative; final pricing by contract)
  - Hosted API (generation): $0.02 per 1k tokens; embeddings: $0.005 per 1k tokens.
  - Dedicated reserved capacity: base committed monthly fee + consumption overage. Example: $10k/month for a small 4-GPU pool (reserved), $40k/month for a medium 16-GPU pool.
  - Private deployment: platform license + professional services; typical initial deployment engagements start at $75k - varies by topology and support SLA.

Pricing table (illustrative)
| Tier           | Hosted rate (gen) | Hosted rate (embed) | Dedicated example cost | Notes |
|---------------|-------------------:|---------------------:|------------------------:|------|
| Small (pilot) | $0.02 / 1k tokens  | $0.005 / 1k tokens  | $10k / month (4 GPUs)  | 30-day pilot available |
| Mid           | $0.018 / 1k tokens | $0.0045 / 1k tokens | $25k / month (8 GPUs)  | Cost optimization review included |
| Enterprise     | custom pricing     | custom pricing      | $40k+ / month (16+ GPUs)| SLA & compliance add-ons available |

Discounting guidance
- Standard commercial play: 10-20% for annual commitments.
- Reserved capacity: scale tier discounts at 6-month and 12-month terms.
- Price exceptions require GTM leader sign-off for >25% discount.

Case studies (sales-ready one-paragraph summaries)
1) Acme Retail - personalization at scale
- Context: Multi-tenant ecommerce platform needed low-latency product recommendations and content generation.
- Outcome: Moved from self-hosted prototype to Redwood Dedicated; 40% reduction in per-call inference cost through batching and caching, and 95th percentile latency improved from 480ms to 120ms. Time-to-production reduced from 8 weeks to 2 weeks.

2) FinSys Inc - regulated private deployment
- Context: Financial services firm required on-prem deployment and HSM-backed KMS for key management.
- Outcome: Private deployment with audit logging and SOC2-ready controls enabled a pilot within 60 days; initial model throughput met SLA with 99.9% availability during the 90-day pilot.

3) HelpDeskNow - knowledge base summarization
- Context: Support center used embeddings and reranking for ticket routing.
- Outcome: Embedding-based reranking reduced average handle time by 20% and increased automated resolution rate by 15%.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise Q&A)
Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: For hosted customers data is stored in regional clusters chosen at onboarding; default retention policy is 30 days for transient inference logs and 365 days for audit logs unless otherwise negotiated. Private deployments keep all data under customer control per deployment contract.

Q: Do you offer encryption at rest and in transit?
A: Yes. All traffic to hosted APIs is TLS 1.2+; data at rest in managed services is encrypted with customer-managed keys where requested (KMS support). Private deployments can integrate with customer HSM/KMS.

Q: What certifications and audits do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and performs annual penetration tests. We provide evidence packages for enterprise compliance reviews and work with customers on attestation for regulated environments.

Q: How do you support private deployments and network isolation?
A: Options include VPC peering, private endpoints, and on-prem appliance bundles. The control plane can be deployed in a private VPC and can be configured to avoid public egress for sensitive workloads.

Q: How is access and identity managed?
A: SSO via SAML/OIDC, role-based access control (RBAC) at token/route level, and audit logging for all administrative actions.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities exist for inference requests?
A: Per-request metadata, token cost breakdowns, model version info, and who initiated the request are available in audit logs. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs.

Q: What data residency controls do you provide?
A: Regional hosting options, private deployments, and explicit data residency contracts for EEA/UK customers.

Q: How are model updates and rollouts handled to prevent regressions?
A: Redwood supports canary, A/B, and automatic fallback rollouts with per-prompt evaluation hooks and regression alerts tied to pre-defined prompt sets.

Technical validation checklist for SEs (quick POC checklist)
1) Determine target workload: QPS, average tokens per request, latency SLOs, model(s) required.
2) Recommend deployment mode: hosted for fast start, dedicated for predictable throughput, private for compliance.
3) Run sample traffic: use our evaluation harness with representative prompts (link to repo) and capture p50/p95/p99 latency and token usage.
4) Apply optimization suggestions: batching policy, prefix caching, and quantization profile.
5) Validate monitoring: connect to console, verify token cost breakdowns and audit log forwarding.

Page ownership and maintenance
- Owner: go-to-market (Ava Chen)
